sectionsUsed: Success Criterion 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): non-text content has a text alternative; pure decoration is implemented so assistive technology can ignore it. Page claims: missing alt text, informative chart, decorative divider, GIFT o1 decorative image.
Success Criterion 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A): all functionality is operable through a keyboard interface. Page claims: teach step 4, unreachable Menu control, GIFT o3.

Success Criterion 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (Level A): if focus can be moved to a component with the keyboard, it can be moved away using only the keyboard. Page claims: keyboard trap definition, date picker, Volume slider, GIFT o1 keyboard trap.
Success Criterion 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA): a keyboard focus indicator is visible. Page claims: teach step 4 visible focus.

Success Criterion 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): controls have labels and a programmatically determinable name and role. Page claims: missing label barrier, search field.

Document conformance requirements table: img with alt="" has role none or presentation; button has implicit role button; a with href has implicit role link; input type=checkbox has implicit role checkbox. Page claims: alt empty skipped, native button and link roles, GIFT o2 role versus element.

1. Author requirements: it is not recommended to set role values that match implicit semantics; 3. Author guidance to avoid incorrect use of ARIA. Page claims: prefer a native element over adding a role.

No ARIA is better than Bad ARIA, Principle 1 (A role is a promise): a div with role=button is a promise that the author also provides the keyboard interactions; unlike HTML input elements, ARIA roles do not cause browsers to provide keyboard behaviors or styling. Page claims: prediction, teach step 3, control B, apply question, GIFT o2 items.
